items.text: The system shall provide a location-specific restaurant discovery experience for signed-in users.
items.annotation_notes: The opening screens show a Columbus-specific discovery page with restaurant listings and recommendation sections, which directly supports a location-aware browsing capability.

claims.claim: The system provides restaurant discovery content for a specific location.
The visible session appears to be signed in through account access.

items.evidence_note: Step 1 shows Columbus, OH discovery content and restaurant sections. Step 2 shows an account menu with Sign Out, supporting signed-in context.
items.rationale: The visible UI supports both location-specific discovery and signed-in account context.

items.text: The system shall expose account actions through a user menu.
items.annotation_notes: The sequence moves from the main page to an opened account dropdown that lists profile and other account destinations, directly showing this capability.

claims.claim: The system exposes account-related actions through a user menu.

items.evidence_note: Step 2 shows a user menu with Profile, My Hit List, Payment Methods, Communication, Help & Feedback, and Sign Out.
items.rationale: The account menu visibly exposes multiple account actions.

items.text: The system shall allow authenticated users to navigate to a dedicated profile settings area.
items.annotation_notes: The ordered flow clearly transitions from the account menu to the profile page, showing direct support for profile-settings navigation.
items.manual_verification_notes: removed condition on the start point of navigation

claims.claim: The user menu provides access to Profile.
The flow reaches a dedicated Profile settings page.

items.evidence_note: The account menu in step 2 includes Profile, and step 3 shows the Profile settings page.
items.rationale: The ordered flow visibly moves from account navigation to a dedicated profile settings area.

items.text: The system shall present existing profile information in editable, prepopulated form.
items.annotation_notes: The profile form already contains values such as name, phone, and email before further edits are made, indicating editable prefilled account data.

claims.claim: The profile page displays prepopulated account information.
The prepopulated information is presented in editable form controls.

items.evidence_note: Step 3 shows editable fields prefilled with name, phone number, and email address.
items.rationale: Existing profile values are visibly shown inside editable input fields.

items.text: The system shall allow users to add or edit a short personal bio in their profile.
items.annotation_notes: The short-bio field is visible and then populated with user-entered text, directly showing support for short free-text profile notes.

claims.claim: The profile contains a short bio input area.
The short bio area can contain user-provided text.

items.evidence_note: Step 3 shows the short bio field, and step 7 shows it populated with 'Love Ramen Noodles'.
items.rationale: The flow visibly supports adding or editing a short profile bio.

items.text: The system shall allow users to record allergies and dietary restrictions as profile preferences.
items.annotation_notes: The profile page includes a dedicated allergies and restrictions section with selectable options, which directly grounds this profile-preference capability.

claims.claim: The profile contains an allergies and restrictions section.
Allergy or restriction preferences can be selected in the profile.

items.evidence_note: The allergies and restrictions section is visible, and Dairy plus Peanuts become selected in later steps.
items.rationale: The UI visibly provides selectable profile preferences for allergies and dietary restrictions.

items.text: The system shall support selecting multiple allergy or restriction tags within the same profile.
items.annotation_notes: The flow first shows Dairy selected and then shows Dairy together with Peanuts, demonstrating multi-selection rather than a single exclusive choice.

claims.claim: The profile supports more than one selected allergy or restriction tag at the same time.

items.evidence_note: Step 9 shows both All Dairy and Peanuts selected at the same time.
items.rationale: The selected tag states visibly demonstrate multi-selection.

items.text: The system shall provide visible information on which dietary preference is activated.
items.annotation_notes: Selected tags change visual state, making active choices distinguishable from inactive ones, which is a visible usability and clarity property of the form.
items.manual_verification_notes: had to change to be independent of specific UI implementation artifacts

claims.claim: Activated dietary preference tags are visually distinguishable from inactive tags.

items.evidence_note: Selected tags are shown with a blue active state while inactive tags remain unhighlighted.
items.rationale: The UI visibly communicates which dietary preferences are active.

items.text: The system shall allow users to add an explanatory note alongside allergies and dietary restrictions.
items.annotation_notes: A dedicated text area for allergy and restriction notes is visible throughout the profile workflow, indicating support for supplementary dietary context.

claims.claim: The allergies and restrictions section includes a text area for an explanatory note.

items.evidence_note: The profile page shows a note field with placeholder text for allergies and restrictions.
items.rationale: Because the requirement asks for a mechanism, the visible text area is sufficient evidence for the observable core.

items.text: The system shall communicate how profile information is used.
items.annotation_notes: The profile page includes explanatory text stating that information is shared with restaurants a user reserves, which directly shows visible usage guidance.

claims.claim: The profile page explains that profile information is shared with restaurants for reservations.
The allergies section explains that dietary information can be communicated in advance.

items.evidence_note: Step 3 includes explanatory text about sharing profile information with restaurants a user reserves. The allergy section also contains explanatory helper text.
items.rationale: The UI visibly communicates the reservation-related purpose of profile information.

items.text: The system shall let users maintain reusable dining preferences that can inform future reservations.
items.annotation_notes: The page framing and explanatory text imply that the stored profile is meant to be reused when dining or reserving, but the later reservation-time application is not shown end to end.
items.manual_verification_notes: the notification of the restaurant may also have to have an UI or at least a email template

claims.claim: The profile page allows dining-related preferences to be edited.
The page frames these preferences as information restaurants may use for reservations.
The preferences are reusable for future reservations after this flow.
claims.note: It is strongly implied by the design.

items.evidence_note: The UI supports editing reusable-looking dining preferences, but future reuse and persistence are not visibly confirmed.
items.rationale: The visible profile preference mechanism is supported, while future reuse remains hidden.

items.text: The system shall support entry of birthday information using structured month, day, and year controls.
items.annotation_notes: The flow visibly demonstrates structured birthday entry.

claims.claim: The birthday field is split into structured month, day, and year controls.
The birthday controls can be populated with a month, day, and year.

items.evidence_note: The birthday controls progress from placeholders to January, 05, and 1980.
items.rationale: The flow visibly demonstrates structured birthday entry.

items.text: The system shall provide a save action for committing profile changes.
items.annotation_notes: The save mechanism is visible; successful commitment is not verified.

claims.claim: The system provides a save action for profile changes.
The save action commits profile changes.
claims.note: It's a trivial backend property strongly implied by frontend.

items.evidence_note: A Save action is visible while profile changes are present, but the screenshots do not show a post-save state or stored outcome.
items.rationale: The save mechanism is visible; successful commitment is not verified.

items.text: The system shall keep account-section navigation available while the user edits profile settings.
items.annotation_notes: The profile can be edited while account-section navigation remains available.

claims.claim: Account-section navigation remains available while profile settings are edited.

items.evidence_note: The left account navigation remains present across the profile editing steps.
items.rationale: The profile can be edited while account-section navigation remains available.

items.text: The system shall preserve saved dining preferences and dietary notes when the user later returns to the profile settings area.
items.annotation_notes: Visible editing support is present, but persistence across a later revisit is not verified.

claims.claim: The user can enter dining preference information in the profile.
The profile provides a visible Save action related to these edits.
Saved dining preferences and dietary notes are preserved when the user later returns to the profile.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows editing preferences and a Save button, but does not show a later return to the profile.
items.rationale: Visible editing support is present, but persistence across a later revisit is not verified.

items.text: The system shall pass saved allergy selections and dietary notes into restaurant-facing reservation information.
items.annotation_notes: Visible profile data entry is supported, while the external reservation information transfer is hidden.

claims.claim: The profile allows allergy selections to be recorded.
The profile includes a field for dietary notes.
Saved allergy selections and dietary notes are passed into restaurant-facing reservation information.
claims.note: It is strongly supported by "Let the restaurant know in advance of any allergies or dietary restrictions"

items.evidence_note: The UI supports entering allergy information and explains reservation context, but actual restaurant-facing delivery is not visible.
items.rationale: Visible profile data entry is supported, while the external reservation information transfer is hidden.

items.text: The system shall allow access to editable profile settings only for the authenticated account owner.
items.annotation_notes: The central owner-only access rule cannot be judged from the captured flow.

claims.claim: Editable profile settings are accessible in an authenticated session.
Access to editable profile settings is limited to the authenticated account owner.

items.evidence_note: The screenshots show profile access in a signed-in session, but they do not test another user, unauthenticated access, or authorization enforcement.
items.rationale: The central owner-only access rule cannot be judged from the captured flow.

items.text: The system shall apply all saved profile dining preferences consistently to every future reservation made from the account.
items.annotation_notes: The universal future-application requirement is not verifiable from these screenshots.

claims.claim: Profile dining preferences can be edited.
All saved profile dining preferences are applied consistently to every future reservation made from the account.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows profile dining preference editing, but no future reservations or consistency checks are shown.
items.rationale: The universal future-application requirement is not verifiable from these screenshots.

items.text: The system shall present an explicit post-save confirmation or summary indicating that profile edits were stored.
items.annotation_notes: The expected visible confirmation or summary is absent in the final visible state after the profile edits.

claims.claim: The system provides an explicit post-save confirmation or stored-edits summary after profile edits.

items.evidence_note: The final relevant screenshot shows the edited profile form and Save button, but no visible confirmation or summary.
items.rationale: The expected visible confirmation or summary is absent in the final visible state after the profile edits.

items.text: The system shall warn users about unsaved profile changes before they leave the editing flow.
items.annotation_notes: The warning condition is not exercised, so the requirement cannot be judged.

claims.claim: Users can create unsaved profile changes.
The system warns users about unsaved profile changes before they leave the editing flow.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows profile edits, but it does not show the user attempting to leave the editing flow before saving.
items.rationale: The warning condition is not exercised, so the requirement cannot be judged.
